newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Cabinet minister says Israel could annex West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Cabinet minister says Israel could annex West Bank.

text.p: Israel's communications minister said on Wednesday Israel should claim sovereignty over the occupied West Bank and Gaza if Yasser Arafat carries out his promise to declare a Palestinian state in two years.

"I will propose imposing Israeli sovereignty over Judea, Samaria and Gaza in the event of such an action," Communications Minister Limor Livnat told parliament, using the biblical names Judea and Samaria for the West Bank employed by the Israeli right.

Earlier this month Arafat, president of the Palestinian Authority in areas given limited self-rule under a peace deal with Israel's previous government, said he would declare a state when an interim phase in current peace accords was over in two years' time.
Livnat, campaign manager when Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was elected in May, said Arafat's comment effectively ended the Oslo accord, the peace agreement with the previous Israeli government.
"What Yasser Arafat said about the unilateral formation of an independent Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital is no longer just a violation of the agreement," she said.
"It's a lot more than that. This declaration effectively means the nullification of the Oslo agreement," Livnat said.
The breakthrough interim peace accord signed by Israel and the PLO in 1993 after secret talks in Norway was opposed by the Israeli right.

Netanyahu has ruled out a Palestinian state or the return of occupied Arab land in exchange for peace. Talks scheduled in the Oslo agreement to reach a final Israeli-Palestinian settlement have not resumed since Netanyahu took office.
Palestinian officials said although the PLO declared a state from exile in 1988, a call now would be more significant because Arafat was in charge of self-rule areas in the West Bank and Gaza.

Israel declared sovereignty over Arab East Jerusalem when it captured it in 1967 along with the rest of the West Bank and Gaza Strip. The claim, recognised by almost no countries, was to be settled during the proposed final status talks.

Israel has also extended its laws over the occupied Golan Heights, captured from Syria during the same 1967 Middle East war, a step widely interpreted as a claim of sovereignty. Netanyahu has rejected any return of the Golan, a basic demand of Syria in peace talks.
